items.question: Does the viewer commit to a wrong answer before hearing the right one?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: Second round failed it twice (the profit/cash lesson stated before the commitment; 'Was it safe?' implied a no the run does not support). Fixed: the viewer now names a number (the biggest bill the business could pay), it is answered with the trough after the Saunders' September beat, and the profit/cash lines moved after the answer; the cold open ends on the resignation, not the cash quote.

items.question: Is there a concrete number in the first sentence?
Is the title's promise fully delivered?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: Both halves delivered: the corner and the date, then 'Find your date'. The three cash claims were checked against run.json by the critic: every quantile of the paths' minimum is $85,242; a payment above it on that day breaks all 10,000; end_p5 is from the same draw.

items.question: Does any notation appear before its intuition?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: Paths are introduced before 'the middle of them'; short selling before the corner's mechanics; the trough shown before it is named.

items.question: Is there exactly one idea, and exactly one CTA?
items.note: 1 CTA beat(s); one idea: Every beat serves 'cash is a date: find your trough and the payment that would break it'; the correlation point is one supported clause.

items.question: Does the CTA match the awareness stage in §8?
Is there one claim a competent operator could dispute?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: 'The rule is measuring the wrong thing' and 'The trough was decided when the orders were placed' are disputable by a competent operator.

items.question: Is there any gap over 40 seconds without a re-hook?
Does every number name its model run?
items.note: every chart beat names its run; every key exists

items.question: Is any step of the method withheld?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: Complete by-hand method: dated outflows, payouts dated from payable day, settlement and bank, the daily balance, the low and its date, the breaking-payment test, the levers, the floor, and now the course's lesson-6 rule (average the worst twentieth of lows).

items.question: Does the close state a real limitation rather than pitch?
items.note: independent critic, two rounds: Real limit (one path isn't the future; demand moves together; lead times slip; dozens of products), the spec's soft close word for word, the free course; cadence aligned to the site's 'every week'.

items.question: Are CLIP markers placed, with at least three usable?
Would a $30M founder outside Amazon still get something from this? (pillars 1–2 exempt)
